title: Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha): design partner selection
creator: Vivek Kulkarni
body:
Goal
Select 1–2 design partners for the "Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha)" program and lock success metrics + timeline. This ticket tracks candidate pipeline, selection criteria, and the operational plan (cadence, support model, and what we commit to during alpha).

Background / why now
In Private technical discovery and pilots, the largest source of variance and delivery risk is customer networking: VPC layout/subnets, DNS, endpoints, NAT strategy, flow logs/auditability, SG boundaries, IAM permission boundaries, and private connectivity integration (VPN/DX). The alpha modules encode Redwood-validated defaults to reduce pilot time and reduce “mystery meat” infra differences that later break the installer.

Alpha scope reminder (for partner screening)
- AWS VPC-based footprint only (EKS assumed in reference architecture)
- Modules cover networking + foundational infra only (VPC/subnets/routes/NAT, endpoints + DNS flags, logging defaults/flow logs, security group patterns, IAM scaffold for installer execution role, optional VPN/DX placeholders)
- Not a turnkey end-to-end install (cluster/app install is handled by redwood-private-installer + Helm)

Selection criteria (must-haves)
1) Architecture fit
- AWS VPC private deployment required (VPC-only; no public cluster requirement)
- Willing to implement the reference architecture closely for alpha (limited customization)
- EKS is acceptable (or they are willing to use EKS for the pilot)

2) Networking characteristics we want in the alpha sample
- One partner with strict egress constraints (endpoints-first, minimal NAT) and a security review process
- One partner with a more standard enterprise VPC (NAT, endpoints, central logging) to validate defaults and docs
- Bonus: partner with VPN/Direct Connect requirements (we’ll validate placeholders + extension points, not full implementation)

3) Operational readiness
- Has a named platform owner and security reviewer (can attend weekly check-ins)
- Can provision AWS account(s) / VPC(s) and run Terraform with minimal back-and-forth
- Will commit to share anonymized logs/screenshots for debugging (or allow screen-share) within compliance constraints
- Can run the pilot inside the planned alpha window (target start in July)

4) Commercial + relationship
- Active opportunity for Redwood Private within 1–2 quarters and strong mutual incentive to unblock
- Comfortable with “alpha” labeling and known limitations; willing to sign alpha addendum / support expectations

Disqualifiers / watch-outs
- Requires bespoke network topology or insists on existing bespoke VPC modules as a hard constraint (unless they accept a “wrapper” approach)
- Non-AWS-first or near-term GCP/Azure requirement as a hard blocker
- Air-gapped/on-prem only with no initial VPC pilot environment
- Cannot allow required endpoints/DNS setup needed by installer

Candidate pipeline (as of 2025-07-08)
A) Acme Bank (regulated, financial services) — STRONG CANDIDATE
- Fit: High. Needs VPC endpoints, audit logs/retention controls, SIEM export. Data residency and strict change control.
- What we learn: Endpoint coverage + private DNS behavior, logging defaults (Flow Logs to customer-owned S3/CloudWatch), IAM boundary posture.
- Risks: Longer security review cycle; may require formal documentation and approvals before any apply.
- Field notes: SE expects this partner to surface the “hard parts” (DNS + endpoints + egress) quickly.
- Proposed pilot environment: Non-prod VPC in customer sandbox account; one region; private subnets only; endpoints enabled; NAT minimized.

B) Northstar Healthcare (regulated-ish, healthcare) — STRONG CANDIDATE
- Fit: High. Focus on strict egress controls and clear day-2 expectations; on-prem future is on roadmap but will start with VPC.
- What we learn: Egress restrictions, operational runbooks (upgrade/rollback), DNS stability in private subnets.
- Risks: Timeline pressure (POC window); may need strong “known limitations” alignment to avoid overpromising.
- Proposed pilot environment: POC VPC with endpoints; standard NAT; central log destination required.

C) (Open slot) Mid-market SaaS platform team — BACKUP CANDIDATE
- Status: SE to propose 1–2 candidates by 2025-07-12.
- Desired characteristics: faster cycle time, fewer compliance gates; validates docs/quickstart quality and "happy path".

Selection decision (proposed)
- Primary design partners: Acme Bank + Northstar Healthcare
- Backup: one mid-market SaaS (if either regulated partner slips in timeline)

Alpha success metrics (what we will measure)
Partner-level success (per partner)
1) Time-to-first-apply
- From “repo created + inputs provided” to successful Terraform apply: <= 2 business days for the customer team (excluding Redwood wait time)

2) Installer readiness
- Installer preflight passes on first attempt OR clear actionable errors (no ambiguous failures)
- Zero P0 networking blockers (e.g., missing ECR endpoints + private DNS misconfig without guidance)

3) Stability + day-2
- Successful upgrade to one newer module version (patch/minor) following runbook
- Drift handling documented (at least one drift scenario exercised or reviewed)

4) Supportability
- < 3 total escalations requiring infra engineering “live debugging” per partner after initial setup
- Docs gaps captured as actionable items (each partner produces a list of “top 5 confusing items”)

Program-level success
- Validate our default topology + extension points across 2 distinct enterprise constraints
- Produce a reusable “Design Partner Pilot Pack”: pinned module versions, example tfvars template, and a standard checklist for networking prerequisites
- Confirm logging/IAM default posture is acceptable to at least one regulated partner’s security team (even if with adjustments documented)

Commitments to partners (alpha contract)
- Weekly 30-minute check-in (SE + PM + Infra/Private deployments as needed)
- Shared Slack channel for pilot support; response targets: best-effort within 1 business day; P0 within 4 business hours during agreed overlap
- Known limitations: AWS-only, limited customization; some changes may be required between alpha releases; partners must pin versions
- Redwood will provide upgrade notes and coordinate any breaking changes (or avoid them during pilot window)

Timeline (target)
- 2025-07-08: Confirm candidate list + send pilot ask email (SE to lead outreach)
- 2025-07-12: Lock partner selection + NDAs / alpha addendum where needed
- 2025-07-15: Kickoff calls (per partner) + access/prereq checklist review
- 2025-07-22: First Terraform apply in partner sandbox + installer preflight
- 2025-08-05: Mid-pilot review: issues + docs gaps + decision on defaults
- 2025-08-19: Upgrade exercise + finalize learnings
- 2025-08-26: Alpha release readiness checkpoint (tie into PM-928)

Open questions
- Do we require a customer-owned S3 bucket for Flow Logs by default for regulated partners, or keep CloudWatch as default with optional S3?
- What is the minimum endpoint set we enforce in docs vs allow installer to warn on (ECR api+dkr, S3 gateway, STS, CloudWatch Logs, etc.)?
- How do we describe private DNS constraints without over-constraining customers (e.g., interactions with existing Route53 Resolver rules / split-horizon DNS)?

Next steps (action items)
1) Rachel: schedule selection review with Vivek + Markus + Irene (30 min) and confirm final pick.
2) Markus (SE): confirm Acme + Northstar pilot dates and identify who owns Terraform applies on customer side.
3) Irene/Victor: provide prereq checklist (endpoints/DNS/NAT expectations) to share pre-kickoff.
4) Naomi/Marcus: provide a 1-pager on logging + IAM boundary posture suitable for partner security review.
